_README: Bus stops along the first bridge, in WORLD coordinates.
Taken straight from the placed SM_SM_Concrete_Base_XXL1 bridge tiles in
the mesh shard, which is already post-offset -- so these need no further
transform and carry world_coords.
Do NOT run OFFSET_* over them. Only OFFSET_Z separates a tile's editor Z
(815) from its world Z (-21365); X and Y come through unchanged. Adding
OFFSET_X/Y as well moved the stops off the bridge entirely, and skipping
OFFSET_Z put them 222 m up. The tiles themselves are the ground truth.
Z is tile Z + 20, so the stop sits on the deck rather than in it.
AdditionalDestinations, together with its siblings. One direction only --
vanilla actors come through the build as byte-copied RawExports, so they
cannot be made to point back.
One stop is a CONTROL placed inside a vanilla zone -- see its _why.
Placement goes through the 'BusStop' entry in bp_registry, on the same
clone path as the parking spaces and delivery points.
link_terminal is DISABLED. With it set, the game crashed with an access
violation the moment a resident boarded a bus -- reading a null at +0x2d8,
in the destination logic. AdditionalDestinations is part of that logic and
no vanilla stop uses it the way we did: one stop, one entry, on a warehouse
(Ae-WolWarehouse). Five stops all pointing at a terminal in another zone was
always the unvalidated experiment here.
Re-enable by naming a terminal, but only once passengers are known to work
without it.

stops.name: Zone Test Gangjung
stops._why: Deliberately inside the Gangjung MTAreaVolume, 40 m from its terminal. The five bridge stops sit in no zone at all and hold 0 passengers forever; this one is the control. If it fills and they stay empty, passengers come from zone residents and the island needs its own MTAreaVolume, not a fix to the stops.
